correctness.rationale: Reconstructed both exact implicit root equations from the stated Ahamed–Roy Corollaries 2.1,2.2. Their difference at equal r factors 2M(2-3r)log(1-r), vanishing in (0,1) only at r=2/3, which evaluates to the displayed M*. Root-level partial derivatives give ∂_M H_j=(1-r)/M>0, ∂_r H_2=1+2M(r/(1-r)-2log(1-r))>0, and ∂_r H_1=(2log2+ε)/(2log2-ε(1+logε))>0 for ε=1-r. Each root is therefore strictly decreasing in M. Sign at r1 pins the strict reversal: r2<r1 for M<M*, and r1<r2 for M>M*. Transformed ε-equations yield 1-r1~4(log2)M and 1-r2~2Mlog(1/M) as M↓0. Taylor series A1(r)=2r-r²/2+O(r³) and A2(r)=3r²/2+O(r³) at zero yield r1~η/(1+4M_c) and r2~η, η=1-M/M_c, M_c=1/[2(log4-1)]. Independent high-precision bisection tested 0.001,0.05,M*,0.3 and respects strict orientation; numerical samples are not used to prove uniqueness or endpoints.

value.rationale: Determining which of two already-sharp universal radius inequalities is quantitatively stronger as the same harmonic-class parameter varies is an intrinsic analytic question introduced by the generalized coefficient-basis framework. The exact unique order reversal and logarithmic-vs-linear endpoint scaling provide a natural complete parameter phase diagram. This is more than reporting numerical root tables or renaming old constants.

final_claim: The two distinct sharp close-to-convex harmonic Bohr radii from arXiv:2606.29810v1 cross once, at r=2/3 and M=1/[2(log192-1)], with a strict ordering reversal and unequal parameter endpoint laws.
limitations: Only two stated sharp radii and 0<M<M_c; no pointwise dominance claim for individual harmonic functions.
